svg.title: In the language of the method, c is the datum that every later readout shares: lattices, clocks, windows and volumes are all read from the same c, and successful estimates obtained on different calendars are never combined. The calendar is not unique. The admissible calendars form a directed family under the enlargements used below (raising a length floor before the lengths are chosen; raising entry delays with the lengths held fixed), and every inequality listed is monotone under those enlargements. This non-uniqueness is a presentation ambiguity: no recovered statement depends on which admissible calendar is used, but each statement is proved on one. Because the calendar contains no group element, its frame lift is the identity, and it is the labelling datum of the realized family in Section 8: the level index i, the stage J(i), the clock bβi and the side Ppdi of every leaf are read from it. Nothing in the admission of the source support produces these numbers; they are realization data chosen by the supplied construction in the stated order.
